1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 3.

The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no. 39/22 (416), 48/2 (214) i.e. total land admeasuring 7 bigha 10 biswas (in short, the said land) having Unknown vs Union Of India on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52467777/
2 share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
5.
It is stated that the compensation awarded by the learned LAC is too low, unjust, arbitrary and assessed without any reasonable basis and the same is not acceptable to the petitioners.
The petitioners are recorded bhumidhars of the said land which has been acquired vide the said order.

LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 The said land is very fertile and also gives handsome income to the petitioners in the form of 34 crops in a year.

6. It is stated that the said land is situated in village Rani Khera and is well connected with roads from all sides at the time of acquisition and was having great potential value for the residential as well as commercial purposes.
The said land is duly levelled and as such gives handsome income to the petitioners.
7. It is stated that the said land is situated near NH10 and is having a great potential value as a perfect building/commercial site.

The building activities and commercial activities is coming up for last more than 15 years and, therefore, the said land has great potential value and the market value of the said land is more than Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

It is stated that all kind of civic amenities i.e. electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college were situated in and around the said land and the said land has great potential value.

8. It is also stated that the said land is approachable by mettled roads and is very close to Mundka Industrial area which is fully developed at the time of issuance of the notification under Section 4 of the Act as adjoining areas have been developed as perfect industrial areas, therefore, the market value of the said land also requires the same status which is perfect for industrial sites just near Mundka Metro Rail Project.

There are many LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 residential colonies in and around the said land,
which shows the great potential value of said land at the time of passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act in as much as the land situated in nearby areas could easily fetch Rs. 10,000 per square yards.
9.

It is stated that the compensation assessed by the learned LAC is not based on the sound reasoning as such the said land has more potential/market value, which is not less than Rs. 10,000 per square yards.
The assessment done by the learned LAC is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be rectified and compensation paid to the petitioners may be enhanced.

10. It is also stated that during the interregnum Sh. Satpal, (father of the petitioner has expired)
before passing of the Award, therefore, the present petitioners are the legal heirs of Sh. Satpal and has filed the present reference petition.
It is prayed that the petitioners may kindly be awarded the compensation of the land @ Rs. 10,000 per square yards along with statutory solatium and interest and other benefits.

3 11.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, it is inter alia,
submitted that ld. LAC while passing the said Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the said sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 available to the ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

12. It is stated that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

13. It is submitted that DDA is not liable to pay compensation for the said land which has been handed over to DDA and subsequently taken back by Land and Building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
It is stated that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award, reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

It is stated that DDA is not liable to pay compensation for the language has not been taken over by the DDA either due to stay order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi or has been handed over to DDA and subsequently taken back by land and building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 14.

It is stated that the possession of the said land has been handed over to DDA on 15.12.2005 and after taking the position, the same has been transferred to RPDVII on 20.12.2005 in terms of Kabza Karwahi report dated 29.11.2017 and out of the total land, the land bearing Khasra number 48//4 (214) has been taken back by land and building Department from DDA and subsequently handed over to DSIDC.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate,
just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioners are not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioners in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioners is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioners is liable to be dismissed with cost.
15. Written statement has not been filed on behalf of DSIDC as well as union of India.
16. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 08.07.2015 : ISSUES.

4
1. Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?OPP 2. Relief.
LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 12 17.
Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
18. Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld.

Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they both are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 titled as Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India of Village Rani Khera.

entities.text: Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India of Village Rani Khera
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
19. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?OPP 20.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
21.
To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
22. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

23. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

Unknown vs Union Of India on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52467777/
5 24.

In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
25. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 26.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 160/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Shradhanand v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 27.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 18th DAY OF MARCH, 2023.
